name: tweet-style-importer
cost: Free (MIT, with a request to keep the author's name and repo link)
works_with: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, WorkBuddy and OpenCode
short: Takes an X post of AI art, saves its images and adds the look to the handraw-style library as a new numbered style with reference grids.
what: This skill is part of handraw-style, a library of 330 numbered hand-drawn styles that turns a style number and a theme into image prompts. Give it a post link and it downloads the post and its full-size images, assigns the next style number, and makes a 1024×1024 four-grid reference, a clean 512×512 single image and a slot on a 16-grid gallery board. It then registers the style, marks it to always pass a reference image to the image model, and rebuilds and checks the gallery.
who: People who use handraw-style and want to grow their copy of the library with styles they find on X. It works on the repo's own files, so it does nothing for you without that library. The SKILL.md is written in Chinese.
needs: The handraw-style repo installed as a skill
Python, to run the import script
A link to an X post with images

steps.title: Install the library
steps.text: The README's install is a request to your agent, which clones the repo and sets up the styles and assets: "Install this Skill for me: https://github.com/yang0/handraw-style".

steps.title: Import a post
steps.text: From the repo folder, run the script with the post's link.

steps.title: Name the style yourself (optional)
steps.text: `--name` sets an English style name and `--traits` a Chinese description of the style.
steps.code: python scripts/import_tweet_style.py "https://x.com/username/status/..." --name "Custom Style Name" --traits "核心特征描述"

steps.title: Look at the gallery
steps.text: The script rebuilds the gallery and runs the library's checks. Open `skills/handdraw-style-prompter/gallery/index.html` to find the new style.

try.label: From the SKILL.md
try.where: Your coding agent, in the repo
try.text: Give it a post link and ask it to add the style to the library. It reports the new number, author, style name and group, with a prompt template in Chinese and English.

watch: It downloads other people's images from X and keeps them in your library. Those images belong to the people who made them.
A post you already imported isn't fetched again. It checks `downloads/tweet_{id}/` first and returns the existing number.
It edits library files: the style table, `references/model_capabilities.json` and the gallery boards.
Neither the README nor the SKILL.md says how the script fetches posts or what it needs installed to do so.
